title: Hair oils explained: amla, bhringraj, castor and how to oil your hair
body:
In India, oiling your hair is a weekly ritual passed down through families: warm oil massaged into the scalp, left to soak in, then washed out. It is one of the simplest ways to make dry hair feel softer and look glossier, and it is easy to start. Here is what the classic ingredients (amla, bhringraj, castor oil and more) bring to a hair oil, how to choose one, and how to oil your hair step by step.

What does a hair oil do?

A hair oil coats the hair shaft, so lengths feel softer, smoother and less frizzy, and look shinier. Used before washing, it cushions the lengths so they feel less dry after shampoo. And the scalp massage that goes with it is relaxing in itself. Think of a hair oil as a conditioning treatment for hair and scalp.

The key ingredients, explained

  • Amla (Indian gooseberry, Emblica officinalis) is the best-known ingredient in Ayurvedic hair care. In an amla hair oil, the dried fruit is steeped in a base oil such as coconut.
  • Bhringraj (Eclipta prostrata) is a herb traditionally used in Indian hair oils, often alongside amla. Bhringraj oil is usually a herbal infusion rather than a pure oil.
  • Castor oil is thick and rich. On its own it can feel heavy, so it works best mixed with lighter oils, which is how you will find it in most blends.
  • Coconut oil is the classic base for Indian hair oils, light enough for the scalp and rich enough for the lengths.
  • Hibiscus, fenugreek and curry leaf are kitchen-garden ingredients that often join amla in traditional blends.
  • Neem, tea tree and peppermint give an oil a fresh, cooling feel on the scalp.
  • Rosemary essential oil adds a herbal scent and is a popular addition to modern blends.

A note on "hair growth" oils

Hair growth oil is one of the most searched hair care terms in the UK, and it is the name several brands give their blends (see them on our hair growth oil page). Be realistic about what any oil can do: it conditions hair and scalp, makes lengths feel softer and helps them look healthier. Hair loss has many causes, from genes to hormones, stress and diet, and no oil can change those. If you notice sudden, patchy or heavy hair loss, speak to your GP.

How to oil your hair, step by step

  1. Start with dry or slightly damp hair, before you wash it.
  2. Warm the oil. Stand the bottle in a bowl of warm water for a few minutes. Coconut-based oils turn solid in a cold bathroom; this melts them again.
  3. Part your hair into sections and apply a little oil along each parting with your fingertips or the applicator.
  4. Massage your scalp for 3 to 5 minutes with your fingertips in small circles, gently, without scratching.
  5. Smooth what is left through the lengths and ends, then comb through with a wide-tooth comb, such as a neem wood comb (£13.99).
  6. Leave it on for at least 30 minutes, or overnight with a towel over your pillow.
  7. Shampoo, and if hair still feels oily, shampoo a second time. Then condition the lengths.

Once or twice a week is plenty for most people.

Hair oil for dry hair

If your hair is dry, focus on the lengths and ends rather than the scalp, and choose a richer blend with coconut and castor oil. Between washes, smooth a single drop over the ends to tame flyaways, or use a lighter leave-in such as Vilvah Anti-Frizz Hair Serum (£28.99). More ideas: hair oil for dry hair and hair serum for frizzy hair.

Washing it out

A gentle shampoo removes oil without leaving hair squeaky and dry. Try Deyga Rice Water Shampoo (from £10.99) or Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo (£15.99, 250ml) with goat milk, jasmine and pea protein. If your scalp tends to flake, Vilvah Herbal Shampoo for Dandruff Control (from £12.99) pairs with the Anti-Dandruff Hair Oil; see all shampoos for dandruff. If flaking or itching does not settle, ask a pharmacist.

Good to know

  • Patch test first, especially with oils that contain essential oils such as tea tree, peppermint, camphor or rosemary.
  • Keep oil away from your eyes, and do not use it on a broken, sore or irritated scalp.
  • Protect your pillow and clothes: oils can mark fabric.
